title: Branches as Pointers and HEAD Navigation
instructions: Answer from the lesson. Short-answer and practical items accept equivalent technically correct wording. Practical responses are graded using the supplied guidance.

questions.prompt: Which statement best matches this lesson’s central idea: Branches as Pointers and HEAD Navigation?

options.text: The topic is only about changing visual appearance and has no effect on software behavior.
The topic removes the need to test, inspect, or verify a change.
A branch is a named pointer to a commit.
The topic guarantees every implementation will behave identically in every environment.

questions.explanation: The lesson’s core concept describes the relevant mechanism and its practical role; the other options make unsupported absolute claims.

questions.prompt: What is the safest first step when applying the lesson in a real project?

options.text: Inspect the current state, reproduce or define the expected behavior, and change one thing at a time.
Make several unrelated changes at once.
Delete configuration and reinstall every tool immediately.
Ignore errors if the UI appears to work.

questions.explanation: Controlled changes and observable evidence make failures easier to diagnose and fixes easier to validate.

questions.prompt: Which risk or limitation is specifically worth remembering for Branches as Pointers and HEAD Navigation?

options.text: The same command or configuration always works identically on every operating system.
Do not confuse switching branches with copying a separate repository.
A successful first run proves the system is secure and correct.

questions.explanation: This limitation is called out in the lesson; platform differences and unverified assumptions should not be ignored.

questions.prompt: In 2–4 sentences, explain how the concept in “Branches as Pointers and HEAD Navigation” helps achieve this goal: Create and switch branches conceptually as pointers.
questions.expected_answer_guidance: A correct response explains the mechanism in the lesson and connects it to the stated learning goal. Equivalent technically correct wording is acceptable.

questions.prompt: Complete a small practice task for “Branches as Pointers and HEAD Navigation”. State what you changed or inspected, the expected result, the actual result, and one limitation.
questions.expected_answer_guidance: Award credit for a relevant artifact or reproducible steps, a clear expected-versus-actual comparison, and a technically sound explanation of a limitation. Accept different valid environments and implementations.
